standard.title: Technological change in everyday life
standard.description: how technological developments changed people's lives at home, and in the ways they worked, travelled and communicated
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y1 (AC9HS1K02): Students compared daily life across generations identifying change and continuity. They used comparative language for change.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how technological developments changed people's lives at home, and in the ways they worked, travelled and communicated.

nodes.label: Technologies past and present
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify technologies from the past and their modern equivalents across multiple categories (transport, communication, home, work) and describe how each has changed.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two technologies from different categories (e.g. transport and communication) that have changed and describe how each changed.
nodes.typical_width: Examine changes in technologies over several generations by comparing past and present objects and photographs across: land, air and sea transport; transistors to digital streaming; communication over long distances; daily home technologies.
wider: Identify technologies used by local First Nations Australians for daily life (food, shelter, transport) and compare these with European technologies used in the same period
Interview a grandparent or familiar elder about the technologies used in their childhood and record the account
nodes.hinge_reason: Students must understand what technologies changed before they can explain how those changes affected people's lives — the effect analysis in Node 2 requires the change baseline.

response_modes.reason: Build a range of technology examples across multiple categories using objects, photographs and elder interviews before moving to effect analysis.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two technologies across different categories that have changed
Describes how each technology changed from past to present

nodes.label: How technology changed daily life
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how specific technological developments changed people's lives at home, at work, in travel and in communication.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how at least one technological development changed at least two aspects of daily life (e.g. how TV changed both home life and communication).
nodes.typical_width: Discuss how changes to transport, communication and work technologies shaped daily life patterns; suggest what patterns of movement and communication would have been like one or two generations ago; compare with today.
wider: Investigate how current communication and transport technologies connect places internationally and compare with connections possible one generation ago
Explore how accessibility to places changed for different groups (e.g. people with disability, people in remote areas) as transport technologies evolved

response_modes.reason: Multiple technology categories (transport, communication, home, work) provide richer causal explanation than focusing on one category alone.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cross-category comparison reveals that technology change affects daily life in interconnected ways — a student who only studies communication misses the transport-connection interaction.
success_criteria: Explains how at least one technology changed at least one aspect of daily life
Uses cause-effect language to describe the relationship between the technology and the change
